ai.literal: Having investigated, without showing partiality, having adhered to justice, towards anyone having deliberated, that which is done indeed is proper rule.
ai.translation: To investigate thoroughly, to show no partiality, to adhere to justice, and to act after careful deliberation towards anyone—this indeed is proper rule.
ai.modern: எதனையும் நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து, யாரிடமும் பாரபட்சம் காட்டாமல், நடுவுநிலைமையோடு பொருந்தி, அனைவரிடமும் தகுந்ததை ஆராய்ந்து செய்வதே சரியான ஆட்சியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essence of a just rule. The ruler must first investigate any matter thoroughly and act without showing personal favoritism. By adhering strictly to justice and carefully deliberating the consequences for anyone involved, the actions taken constitute true and proper governance. The word 'iṟai' has multiple meanings including king or god, but here it specifically means impartial justice, which is the core duty of sovereignty.

ai.literal: Looking at the sky living world all, king's scepter looking at living subjects.
ai.translation: All the world lives looking to the sky for rain; the subjects live looking to the king's scepter for justice.
ai.modern: உலகத்து உயிர்கள் எல்லாம் மழையை எதிர்பார்த்து வாழ்கின்றன; அதுபோல மக்கள் மன்னனது செங்கோலை எதிர்பார்த்து வாழ்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a parallel between the natural order and the political order. Just as all life on earth depends on the sky for rain to survive, the citizens of a kingdom depend on the king's righteous scepter for justice and security. The word 'kōl' (scepter) symbolizes the ruler's fair administration. Without rain, the world perishes; without a just rule, the society perishes.

ai.literal: To the sages' texts and to virtue, having become the basis, it stands, the king's scepter.
ai.translation: The king's scepter stands as the foundation for both the texts of the sages and virtue itself.
ai.modern: அந்தணர்களின் அறநூல்களுக்கும், தர்மத்திற்கும் அடிப்படையாக நிலைத்து நிற்பது மன்னவனின் செங்கோல் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the foundational role of just governance in a society. The king's scepter (கோல்) symbolizes his righteous rule and authority. It stands as the basis (ஆதி) for both the moral texts of the sages and the actual practice of virtue (அறம்). Without a just ruler to maintain order and protect the good, neither moral teachings nor virtuous deeds can survive and flourish.

ai.literal: Subjects having embraced, scepter who wields, great earth king's, feet having embraced, will stand world.
ai.translation: The world will stand embracing the feet of the king of the vast earth, who wields his scepter while embracing his subjects.
ai.modern: தன் குடிமக்களை அன்போடு அரவணைத்து செங்கோல் செலுத்தி ஆட்சி செய்யும் பெரிய நிலப்பரப்பை ஆளும் மன்னனின் அடிகளை உலக மக்கள் தழுவி நிற்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the reciprocal relationship between a just ruler and the people. The word 'தழீஇ' (having embraced) is used twice to highlight this mutual bond. First, the king rules by embracing his subjects, which means he governs with care and protects their welfare. In return, the world will stand embracing his feet, demonstrating their enduring loyalty and devotion to his righteous rule.

ai.literal: According to rule scepter wielding king in the country, rain and harvest having gathered [will be].
ai.translation: In the land of a king who wields his scepter justly, rain and harvest will gather together.
ai.modern: நீதியின்படி செங்கோல் செலுத்தி ஆட்சி செய்யும் மன்னவனது நாட்டில், மழையும் விளைச்சலும் ஒருசேரக் கூடியிருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects the justice of a ruler with the natural prosperity of his land. The phrase 'இயல்புளி கோல் ஓச்சும்' describes a king who wields his scepter according to the proper nature of justice. In such a king's country, the natural elements respond favorably. Rain ('பெயல்') and agricultural yield ('விளையுள்') will gather together ('தொக்கு'), meaning they will be abundant and timely. The poem suggests that righteous governance brings about ecological and economic harmony.

ai.literal: Spear is not victory that which gives king's; scepter, and that does not bend if.
ai.translation: It is not the spear that brings victory to a king, but his scepter, provided it does not bend.
ai.modern: ஒரு மன்னனுக்கு வெற்றியைத் தருவது அவனுடைய வேல் அல்ல; அவனது செங்கோல்தான், அதுவும் வளையாமல் நேராக இருந்தால் மட்டுமே.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts military might with just governance. The word 'வேல்' (spear) represents the king's weapons and army, while 'கோல்' (scepter) symbolizes his rule and justice. The text states that true victory comes not from armed force but from the scepter. The crucial condition is 'கோடாது எனின்' (if it does not bend), meaning the rule must remain strictly impartial and just. Thus, a king's ultimate success rests on his unwavering commitment to fairness rather than his capacity for violence.

ai.literal: King protects world all; him justice will protect, without-failing if-[he]-does.
ai.translation: The king protects the entire world, and his own justice will protect him if he administers it without failing.
ai.modern: உலகம் முழுவதையும் அரசன் காப்பாற்றுவான்; அவன் நீதி தவறாமல் ஆட்சி செய்தால், அந்த நீதியே அவனைக் காப்பாற்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the reciprocal relationship between a ruler and justice. While it is the king's duty to protect the entire world, he is in turn protected by the very justice ('முறை') he upholds. The phrase 'முட்டாச் செயின்' emphasizes that this ultimate protection is guaranteed only if he administers his duties flawlessly and without any hindrance.

ai.literal: With easy access not examining, justice not doing king, by diminished state by himself will perish.
ai.translation: A king who does not examine cases with easy accessibility and fails to administer justice will fall into a diminished state and perish on his own.
ai.modern: எளிதில் அணுகக்கூடிய நிலையில் இருந்து வழக்குகளை ஆராயாமலும், நீதி வழங்காமலும் இருக்கும் அரசன், தன் வலிமை குன்றிய நிலையில் தானாகவே அழிந்து போவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the inevitable downfall of an inaccessible and unjust ruler. The phrase 'எண்பதத்தான்' (with easy access) acts as an instrumental adverb modifying the negative actions of not examining ('ஓரா') and not doing justice ('செய்யா'), indicating a king who fails to be approachable to his people. Consequently, he is reduced to 'தண்பதத்தான்' (a diminished or 'cooled' state of lost power), leading him to perish entirely on his own ('தானே கெடும்') without needing external enemies to defeat him.

ai.literal: Subjects' protection having guarded, having cherished, fault punishing, blemish is not, king's duty.
ai.translation: Guarding and cherishing the subjects, and punishing their faults, is not a blemish but the duty of a king.
ai.modern: குடிமக்களைக் காப்பாற்றிப் பேணி, அவர்கள் செய்யும் குற்றங்களைத் தண்டிப்பது அரசனுக்குப் பழியாகாது; அது அவனுடைய கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core responsibility of a ruler regarding justice. The words 'காத்து' (guarding) and 'ஓம்பி' (cherishing) emphasize that a king must first protect and care for his subjects. When subjects commit crimes, 'கடிதல்' (punishing or removing the fault) becomes necessary. The text clarifies that such punishment is not a 'வடு' (blemish or cruelty) but rather the essential 'தொழில்' (duty) of a just king.

ai.literal: By murder cruel people king punishing green crop weed with the act of removing equal.
ai.translation: A king punishing cruel murderers is equal to weeding a green crop.
ai.modern: அரசன் கொலைக்குற்றம் புரியும் கொடியவர்களைத் தண்டிப்பது, பசுமையான பயிரைக் காக்க அதிலுள்ள களைகளைப் பிடுங்கி எறிவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares a king's duty of punishing violent criminals to a farmer's duty of weeding a field. The phrase 'கொலையின் கொடியாரை' refers to individuals who are cruel through acts of murder, threatening the safety of others. The 'பைங்கூழ்' (green crop) represents the innocent citizens, while the 'களை' (weeds) represents these dangerous criminals. Just as removing weeds is necessary for the crop to thrive, a ruler's strict punishment of the wicked is a necessary act of justice to protect society.
